_what_this_is: MACHINE-GENERATED, by Claude, from the filmstrips in labelpack/pack_1mp4.
NOT human ground truth. Kept separate from any human labels for that reason,
Scope is deliberately narrower than the pack asks for. The pack asks 'what
kind of action' against 17 classes. At 480x220, from six sampled frames, the
technique is not reliably readable - a jab and a cross are the same few
pixels - so only a strike/none verdict plus a family where it is visible is
recorded here. Guessing the technique would have produced exactly the
confident-but-wrong labels this project has measured the cost of before.
The 40 quiet candidates are COMPLETE and every one was looked at.
The 101 event candidates are NOT - 8 were sampled, 93 remain unlabelled.
_findings: All 40 quiet candidates are genuinely `none` for the boxed fighter. The
heuristic that mined them (no detected action within a margin) held up on
every one, which is worth knowing because tools/mine_own_negatives.py calls
its output a floor rather than ground truth.
But three things are wrong with them as *fighter* negatives:
* 7 of 40 have the box on the REFEREE at the marked moment - white shirt,
dark trousers, standing between the fighters during a break. They are
negatives of an official, not of an athlete.
* 2 have a narrow degenerate box that does not enclose a person.
* 2 are not quiet at all - the OPPONENT throws a visible kick while the
boxed fighter does nothing. `none` is still the right answer for the
boxed fighter, but these are hard negatives, not idle ones.
Of the 8 event candidates sampled, not one clearly matched its proposed
technique, and two were proposed as punches while the filmstrip shows a
kick. That is consistent with the detector being 29% precise.
